correctness.rationale: For a directed union of left submodules over the stated field, basis elements of a finite-dimensional test space in Sym(M)#A involve finitely many polynomial variables. They all lie in one stage, and the stage's equivariant symmetric-algebra inclusion preserves the action and dimensions in its nonzero finite-dimensional Følner witness. Theorem 3.1 of Bartholdi, under the stated cocommutative Hopf hypotheses, supplies submodule, quotient and extension closure and hence finite direct sums; the zero module is extensively amenable as Sym(0)=k. An arbitrary sum is a quotient of a coproduct of extensively amenable submodules, so the largest submodule exists. Image closure gives functoriality; hereditary restriction is T(L)=L intersect T(M) for L contained in M, and the preimage of a nonzero extensively amenable submodule of M/T(M) contradicts maximality by extension closure. No computation is required. The theorem is correct; the claim in the prior-work paragraph that Bartholdi does not state arbitrary direct-sum closure is false. Also, arbitrary colimit closure is an immediate further consequence of coproduct and quotient closure, although not part of the Finding.
